title: Are We Getting More Allergic To Things?

blanks.sentence: Mia has more than 50 allergies, including all nuts and their _____.
She cannot eat most fish, except cooked tuna and cooked _____.
Before going to a restaurant, she needs to speak to the manager and the _____.
The restaurant must follow rules to avoid allergen _____ with her food.
Social situations can be difficult because she does not want to feel like a _____.
Australia is described as the allergy _____ of the world.
Research shows that almost one in ten Australian _____ have an allergy.
Allergy rates show a clear _____ as children grow older.
One possible treatment is to build up a baby’s _____.

multipleChoice.question: What makes Mia’s situation unusual compared with many people who have allergies?
options: She has allergies only during certain seasons.
She has a very large number of allergies.
She is mainly allergic to dairy products.
She became allergic only as an adult.

multipleChoice.question: Why does Mia contact restaurants before visiting them?
options: To ask whether they offer cheaper meals.
To check whether they can meet her dietary safety needs.
To request a private room for her friends.
To explain why she does not eat dairy.

multipleChoice.question: Why are restaurant protocols important for Mia?
options: They help staff prepare meals faster.
They make it easier for Mia to choose from the menu.
They reduce the chance of allergens reaching her food.
They allow Mia to avoid speaking to the chef.

multipleChoice.question: What is Mia worried about when socialising?
options: Her friends may not understand medical advice.
Her friends may feel that her needs cause trouble.
Restaurants may not allow her to bring friends.
She may have to explain allergies to strangers.

multipleChoice.question: Why is Australia called the allergy capital of the world?
options: It has the most allergy doctors.
It is famous for allergy research.
It has especially high allergy rates.
It has the strictest food rules.

multipleChoice.question: What does Frances Mao say about allergies among Australians as they get older?
options: The percentage becomes lower with age.
Food allergies become more serious.
Respiratory allergies disappear completely.
Adults are more likely to develop allergies than infants.

multipleChoice.question: What does “or so” show when talking about age six?
options: The speaker is giving an approximate number.
The speaker is correcting a previous mistake.
The speaker is comparing two age groups.
The speaker is giving a scientific definition.

multipleChoice.question: What is one method scientists are studying to reduce allergies?
options: Giving babies vitamin D.
Avoiding restaurants completely.
Testing adults every six years.
Removing dairy from children’s diets.

multipleChoice.question: How does immunotherapy work according to the programme?
options: Children are kept away from all allergens.
Children receive small amounts of the allergen gradually.
Babies take medicine only after an allergic reaction.
Doctors replace food allergies with respiratory allergies.

multipleChoice.question: What is the overall picture given about allergies in this episode?
options: Allergies are becoming more common, but researchers are exploring ways to manage them.
Allergies mainly affect adults and are usually easy to avoid.
Most allergies are caused by poor restaurant safety rules.
Australia has solved the problem of childhood allergies.
